answer: Each work receipt is hashed and sealed before its result goes public, so a copier cannot read a peer's answer first. A second submission tied to the same sealed receipt forfeits the bond, and that bond sits frozen in a vault until the epoch closes. Jurors are drawn from unrelated subnets and their verdicts carry a quartz-clock signature, so a stale seat cannot be reused. A farm pays one bond per replay plus a fresh seat, while the timber of honest history is the only thing that compounds.
